title: 2014 Sugar Bowl: Trevor Knight and OU Stun Alabama 45-31
question: Who won the 2014 Sugar Bowl between Oklahoma and Alabama?
answer: Oklahoma won, beating No. 3 Alabama 45-31 on January 2, 2014, in New Orleans. Freshman quarterback Trevor Knight threw for 348 yards and four touchdowns and was named MVP.
summary: No. 11 Oklahoma upset No. 3 Alabama 45-31 in the Jan. 2, 2014 Sugar Bowl as freshman QB Trevor Knight threw four TDs and set a Sugar Bowl completions record.
body: Few OU bowl wins have aged as well as this one. Alabama had won the previous two national championships and arrived at the Superdome ranked third. Bob Stoops' Sooners were 10-2 and ranked 11th, and Stoops declined to name a starting quarterback before the game. Freshman Trevor Knight took the first snap.

Knight played the game of his life. He completed a Sugar Bowl-record 32 passes for 348 yards and four touchdowns, two of them covering more than 40 yards, after completing only 47 passes all season. His scoring throws went to Lacoltan Bester, Jalen Saunders twice, and Sterling Shepard.

The defense made Alabama pay for every mistake. Two AJ McCarron interceptions set up Oklahoma touchdowns on the very next play, and the Sooners forced four turnovers overall. Eric Striker tied a Sugar Bowl record with three sacks, and in the final minute he stripped McCarron. Geneo Grissom scooped up the loose ball and returned it 8 yards for the clinching touchdown.

The win lifted OU to 11-2 and, according to the Sugar Bowl, gave the Sooners their fifth Sugar Bowl victory in seven trips to New Orleans. It also gave Stoops a memorable reply to the debate he had stirred the previous offseason, when he called talk of SEC superiority "propaganda."
